newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas up late on cash, technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas up late on cash, technicals.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures scored more gains late Wednesday in moderate trade, boosted by reports of slightly firmer Gulf Coast cash prices and some technical buying when May broke resistance.
At 1340 EDT, May climbed 5.4 cents to the day's high of $1.99 per million British thermal units. June was 5.5 cents higher at $2.03. Other deferreds were up by one to 3.7 cents.

"There was a lot of bullish talk this morning. People are trying to kick funds out of short positions. They're looking for paper (buy stops), and a (May) break above $1.99 could take us to $2.05," said one New York-based futures trader.

Technical traders noted May broke minor resistance at $1.975 this morning, but most agreed it would take a close above $1.99-2.00 to trigger more short covering and new buying. Further selling was expected at $2.05 and $2.095, with support at $1.925, $1.88, $1.85 and $1.825.
Chart watchers noted that June, which rallied this morning to a four-week high of $2.04, broke a double top at $2.03, possibly setting the stage for more upside.
A Reuter poll showed most expected a 5-15 bcf weekly draw when AGA storage data are released later today. For the same week last year, stocks fell by 13 bcf.
Temperatures throughout most of the East and upper Midwest were expected to remain below-normal through the week.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were talked a couple of cents higher early Wednesday to near the $2 level. Midcontinent pipes were little changed in the mid-$1.80s. Gas at the New York city gate was quoted up slightly to the mid-to-high $2.30s.
NYMEX said 26,069 Hub contracts traded at 1320 EDT.
As of 1340 EDT, no NYMEX Permian or Alberta natgas futures were traded.
On the KCBT, May gained six cents to $1.87, while deferreds were steady to up 4.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.7 cent to 12.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
